The project identifies MapDB as both an embedded Java database engine and a collections library with off-heap and on-disk storage.

Elexon's historical assessment identifies the parties as electricity distributors and meter operator agents in Great Britain and describes the agreement's safety, technical, and business interface requirements. The draft is broadly relevant but vague about jurisdiction and conflates the agreement's scope with the separate BSC appointment and qualification process.
Microsoft illustrates partial interface localization over a base or parent language for Windows Language Interface Packs; this is not equivalent to a fully localized language pack.
The vendor identifies ModelSim as an HDL simulator used to verify hardware descriptions.
Rapid7 describes the on-premises Security Console's vulnerability scanning and management role. The example stays within defensive review and remediation.
Nutanix names Calm as the previous name of NCM Self-Service and describes blueprint-based provisioning and application lifecycle orchestration across hybrid clouds.
The operator documents OpenTok as an embeddable realtime communications Video API with audio/video and other collaboration features.
Oracle documents enterprise integration through reference process models, shared service inventory, and service artifacts.
Oracle explicitly identifies Clinical as a clinical data management system and describes entry, validation, and discrepancy management.
Apryse's Java reference lists PDF rendering, conversion, editing, and annotation classes in the PDFNet-associated package, including support for document comments and annotations.
The official project identifies Phalcon as a full-stack PHP web framework distributed as a native C extension; this is more precise than the draft's in-part implementation wording.
The product owner describes workload replication, disaster recovery, and failover testing. This is Protect, not the separate migration product.
